newsitem.title: USA: Virginia to execute man for murder and torture.
newsitem.headline: Virginia to execute man for murder and torture.

text.p: A Virginia man who abducted, tortured and murdered a 15-year-old boy was due to be executed by lethal injection Thursday night at the Greensville Correctional Centre.

Michael Carl George, 39, was convicted of the June 16, 1990, robbery and murder of Alexander Sztanko, whose genitals were burned with a stun gun. Lawyers for George did not file a clemency petition with Gov. George Allen.

George was due to die shortly after 9 p.m. EST. His execution would be the first in Virginia this year and put the state in joint second place with Florida with 38 executions since the death penalty was reimposed nationwide in 1976. Texas, with more than 100, leads the country, but last year Virginia executed eight people -- more than any other state

Sztanko's parents reported him missing the night of June 16, 1990. The next day a police officer spotted George and found Sztanko's tennis shoes nearby. A bloodhound followed the boy's scent to George's Ford Bronco and then to the body.

The boy was shot once in the head and his penis burned while he was still alive, and semen was found on his body. No trace of his wallet and two $20 bills his parents thought he was carrying were ever found.

Searches of George's vehicle and home turned up handcuffs, the 9mm handgun used to kill Sztanko, a stun gun capable of causing the burns suffered by Sztanko and a map with the locations of Sztanko's body and his motorcycle marked.
